newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 11.

text.p: The Health Ministry confirmed on Monday that Stephen Anderson, who is charged with the shotgun murder of Hendrick Van de Wetering at Raurimu, had received treatment from mental health services. Further charges were pending against Anderson, 22, after the deaths of six people -- one of them Anderson's father -- in the central North Island village on Saturday, police confirmed. Six were wounded, one critically. In an unprecedented move on Monday, the ministry issued a statement confirming that Anderson received treatment in Wellington. Page 1.

The Cabinet cut its cashline to the embattled Aotearoa Television Network on Monday, citing "serious reservations" about the station's financial management and controls. It pledged, however, to continue to promote the Maori language through broadcasting, setting a June deadline for finding a long-term solution. Page 1.

Twenty-three jobs in the Conservation Department's Wellington head office are expected to go under restructuring. A department official disclosed the cutbacks on Monday night, commenting on a staff letter on Monday to chief executive Bill Mansfield critical of the restructuring process. Page 2.

The Cook Islands Government has still not made provisions to pay the NZ$6.5 million it owes the Government Superannuation Fund, but high commissioner Iaveta Short said on Monday it would be paid. The fund highlighted the Cook Islands debt in the fund's briefing papers to the incoming government last month.

Associate Treasurer John Delamere has defended his refusal to sit with Labour leader Helen Clark on Waitangi Day during a welcome on the lower marae at Waitangi. Delamere, the MP for Te Tai Rawhiti, said on Monday that Clark, being a woman, should not have sat on the front bench reserved for speakers. The speaker's bench is traditionally a male-only preserve. Page 2.

Aotearoa Television director Morehu McDonald criticised the media for focusing on his, and NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan's, spending on clothing, and said he accepted only part of the blame for the government's decision to stop funding the station. McDonald, speaking at the company's Newmarket office after staff were told of the decision, said he was very disappointed and hoped some way could be found for the decision to be reversed. Page 3.

There could be a backlash by the gun lobby against efforts to tighten gun laws, but the government would not bow to extremists, Police Minister Jack Elder said on Monday. In the wake of the weekend's massacre at Raurimu, in which six people were shot dead, Elder said he personally favoured toughening up gun laws. Page 3.

A Fletcher Construction-led consortium has won the $200 million Electricity Corporation contract to bore the 9.6-kilometre second tailrace at Manapouri. The 43-month project will use a purpose-built 10-metre boring machine to penetrate the solid rock, and will employ more than 200 people at its peak. Fletcher's partners in the landmark engineering feat will be American construction giant Dillingham and Austrian tunnelling specialists Ilbau Gesellshaft. Page 9.

The number of jobs advertised in Wellington in January fell by 0.2 percent from the number advertised in December. Figures compiled by the ANZ Bank show January's figure was down almost 17 percent on a year ago, at under 2,200. However, the trend was less sharp than in previous months. Page 9.
